title: 8 Specialized AI Model Types
about: Human page and this machine-readable file share one source. Each model type lists its pipeline, concrete examples, and living catalogs: databases that keep listing new examples as they are released. A single scenario runs through all 8 types in order so their roles connect.
unifying_idea: All 8 follow the same shape: encode an input into vectors, transform those vectors, decode them into an output. They differ along five dimensions: the unit they think in, what goes in, what comes out, the architectural trick, and how big they are.

scenario.title: The leaking dishwasher
scenario.setup: A customer opens a support app, snaps a photo of a puddle under their dishwasher, and types: "Water everywhere after every cycle. It's a 2021 model, I think it's still under warranty. Can someone come fix it?" The 8 model types below handle the request in order, each passing something to the next.
scenario.outcome: Within one reply the customer gets a plain explanation (torn door gasket), a part already ordered under warranty, and a technician booked. No single model did that; the chain did.

models.name: Large Language Model
models.summary: Predicts the next token of text, one at a time, using a large transformer. The general-purpose reasoner and writer.
models.how: Text is split into tokens (word pieces), each token becomes a vector, and stacked transformer layers let every token attend to every earlier one. The final layer scores every possible next token; one is picked, appended, and the loop repeats.

dimensions.trick: self-attention over all previous tokens, trained on next-token prediction at huge scale

models.scenario_role: Takes everything gathered so far (the diagnosis, the repair steps, the warranty rule) and writes the friendly reply the customer actually reads.
models.passes_on: a drafted reply plus a plan: confirm warranty, order gasket, book visit

models.name: Large Concept Model
models.summary: Reasons over whole sentences as single "concepts" instead of word pieces, so it plans at the level of ideas.
models.how: Text is split into sentences and each sentence is mapped into SONAR, a language-independent sentence-embedding space. The model then predicts the next sentence embedding (Meta's best variant uses diffusion to do this), and a decoder turns that embedding back into a sentence in any supported language.

dimensions.input: text or speech, in many languages
dimensions.output: text or speech, in many languages
dimensions.trick: predicts the next sentence embedding instead of the next token

models.scenario_role: Reads the 60-page service manual for that dishwasher model and condenses the gasket-replacement section into five ordered steps, without getting lost in word-level detail.
models.note: This is the youngest type here; the catalogs mostly list research papers rather than ready-to-use models.

models.name: Large Action Model
models.summary: Turns a goal into actions in the real world: clicking, calling APIs, filling forms. The model that does things, not just says things.
models.how: It perceives the current state (a screen, an API response), recognizes the intent, breaks the goal into steps, and emits structured actions such as function calls. Memory tracks what already happened, symbolic rules keep actions valid, and the result of each action feeds back into the next decision.

dimensions.input: goal plus observed state (screens, API results)
dimensions.trick: trained on action trajectories and function-calling data, with a perceive, act, observe loop
dimensions.size: small to large; often an LLM fine-tuned for tools

models.scenario_role: Executes the plan: looks up the order to confirm warranty, places the gasket order, and books the earliest technician slot in the scheduling system.
models.passes_on: confirmation numbers for the part and the visit

models.name: Mixture of Experts
models.summary: A big model where only a few specialist sub-networks run for each token, so it has the knowledge of a huge model at the cost of a small one.
models.how: Inside each layer, a small router network scores every expert for the current token, keeps the top K (often 2 of 8, or 8 of 256), runs only those, and blends their outputs by the router's weights. Most parameters sit idle for any given token.

dimensions.input: text (or any modality the base model takes)
dimensions.trick: sparse routing: only the top-K experts run per token
dimensions.size: huge total parameters, small active parameters

models.scenario_role: Is how the LLM step is served affordably. When the reply mentions warranty law, the router sends those tokens to experts that learned legal text; appliance vocabulary goes to others.
models.passes_on: the same reply, produced at a fraction of the compute

models.name: Vision-Language Model
models.summary: Looks at images and reads text together, then answers in language. An LLM that can see.
models.how: A vision encoder turns the image into patch vectors, a projection layer maps them into the same space as the language model's token vectors, and the language model reads image patches and text tokens side by side to generate an answer.

dimensions.trick: a projection layer that lets a language model read vision features as if they were tokens
dimensions.size: 1 billion to hundreds of billions of parameters

models.scenario_role: Looks at the photo with the masks from SAM plus the customer's words and states: "The lower-left door gasket is torn; water is escaping there, not from the hose."

models.name: Small Language Model
models.summary: A compact language model, usually under about 10 billion parameters, built to run fast and privately on a phone, laptop or edge device.
models.how: Same next-token idea as an LLM, but with fewer, leaner layers, trained on carefully curated data or distilled from a larger model, then quantized (for example to 4-bit numbers) so it fits in device memory.

dimensions.trick: distillation, curated data and quantization to fit on-device

models.scenario_role: Runs on the customer's phone before anything is uploaded: strips the home address and phone number from the message and tells the customer "Got it, analyzing your photo" instantly, even on a weak signal.
models.passes_on: a redacted message and the photo

models.name: Masked Language Model
models.summary: Reads a whole passage in both directions at once and fills in hidden words. Not a writer; an understander, used for search, classification and embeddings.
models.how: During training some tokens are hidden and the model predicts them from the words on both sides. After training, the prediction head is usually dropped and the rich per-token or per-sentence vectors are used to classify text or find similar text.

dimensions.trick: bidirectional attention trained by filling in masked words

models.scenario_role: Classifies the ticket (category: appliance repair, urgency: high, sentiment: frustrated) and embeds it to find the three most similar solved tickets and the right manual for that model number.
models.passes_on: ticket labels, similar past cases, the correct manual

models.name: Segment Anything Model
models.summary: Given an image and a hint (a click, a box, a word), outlines exactly which pixels belong to the object. It cuts things out; it does not name them.
models.how: A heavy image encoder runs once to turn the image into an embedding. A light prompt encoder turns each click or box into vectors, and a fast mask decoder correlates the two to output a pixel mask, so new prompts on the same image are nearly instant.

dimensions.input: image plus prompt (point, box, mask, or text in newer versions)
dimensions.trick: encode the image once, then answer many cheap prompts against it

models.scenario_role: Outlines the puddle, the door gasket, and the drain hose in the photo so the next model knows exactly which regions to look at.
models.passes_on: three labeled masks over the photo
